test_title: PYST 06: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 08 Oct, 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in phrasal verb.

Tara was late for the meeting / but somehow managed / to catch out with / everything she had missed.

options.text: Tara was late for the meeting

solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. to catch out with .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct phrasal verb in this context should be **“catch up with”** rather than “catch out with.”
 
• “Catch up with” means to reach someone or something by moving faster, or to reach the same level or standard as someone or something else.
 
• The sentence should be corrected to maintain proper usage of the phrasal verb and convey the intended meaning clearly.

Correct sentence: *Tara was late for the meeting but somehow managed to **catch up with** everything she had missed*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commonly Confused Phrasal Verbs:**

 
 
• **Catch on:** To understand or realize something. *It took him a while to catch on to the joke.*
 
• **Catch out:** To unexpectedly find out something, often a mistake. *The teacher caught the student out in a lie.*
 
• **Catch up:** To reach the same level or position as others. *She had to stay late to catch up on her work.*
